$schema-note: Which of the four skills each reference file belongs to. Written BEFORE anything moves, so the assignment is reviewable on its own and the migration that follows is mechanical.
why: description plus when_to_use share one ~1536 char cap per skill (skills.md:327-328), and 27 reference subjects competed for one description. Description space buys invocation, and invocation is the largest measured effect in the benchmark: 26 of 36 questions opened the library in the 2026-08-15 run, and cells that opened it scored 5.59 of 6 against 4.23 for cells that did not. Four skills means four budgets.
seam: Partition the COLLISION WORDS, the nouns a question can name that appear in more than one subject. Scored against the repo's own routing table by reusing parseRoutingRows: the trigger-noun seam lands a row's destinations inside exactly one skill for 98% of rows, against 95% for the layer/taxonomy seam the SKILL.md body proposes. The layer seam leaks because it classifies artifacts; a question names a noun.
risk: The listing budget drops descriptions starting with the LEAST invoked skills (skills.md:1047). Four new skills have zero invocation history, so they are the most droppable entries the moment they ship. Intended outcome: more usable description budget. Plausible failure: four name-only skills, strictly worse than one. Part D of the plan re-runs the benchmark against a pre-committed revert condition rather than assuming.

duplicatedIntoEverySkill.why: These four are navigation and provenance, not subject matter, and a reader who lands in one skill needs them there. CORRECTED 2026-08-19 by independent review: this said duplication was cheap because all four carry ZERO claims, which is false at HEAD, where selection.md carries 1, composition-cards.md 1 and sources.md 2, all ledgered. Duplicating them therefore DOES collide CLM-* ids across copies, and verify-evidence now fails on a duplicate extraction id rather than silently dropping one of the pair. Before cutover either strip the tags from those four lines or give each skill copy its own id namespace.
duplicatedIntoEverySkill.cost: It contradicts this repo's own stated principle that a duplicated list is a second place for the truth to rot. Mitigated by a byte-identity gate against the canonical copy rather than by hoping.

invariants: Every file in references/ appears exactly once across skills.files, or in duplicatedIntoEverySkill.
No file appears in both places.
No two skills share a collision word.
Every listed file exists on disk.

skillMdClaims.$why: SKILL.md becomes four files, so its six claims need a home each. The three table-row claims follow their subject. The three tag-legend claims are ONE legend, not four: verify-evidence re-runs the extraction and diffs by record, so prose repeated in four SKILL.md files would yield four claims and a ledger that has to carry them. The legend therefore lives in exactly one SKILL.md and the other three point at it in words that contain no bracketed tag token, because a bracketed token is what the extractor keys on.
